items.title: Sodium burns to make table salt — and then keeps wanting to react
items.claim: Sodium chloride formation looks like the textbook ionic reaction. Yet ionising Na to Na+ (+496 kJ/mol) and adding electron to Cl (-349 kJ/mol) gives a net cost of +147 kJ/mol. Why does it happen at all?
items.prompt: Where does the energy come from?

options.text: From the heat of the burning reaction
The lattice enthalpy — the enormous release of energy when Na+ and Cl- assemble into the crystal (around minus 787 kJ/mol) — dwarfs the cost of making the ions
From nowhere — the reaction is technically not spontaneous

items.reveal:
The full Born-Haber cycle for NaCl: atomise Na (+107), atomise Cl (+122), ionise Na (+496), add electron to Cl (-349), assemble lattice (-787). Net: -411 kJ/mol — exothermic and spontaneous.

Ionic bonding is NOT 'Na giving an electron to Cl' as the simple GCSE diagram suggests. It's the electrostatic stabilisation of a 3D crystal lattice. Lose the lattice (e.g., dissolve in water), and the bond is gone. NaCl(s) is stable; isolated NaCl molecules barely exist outside the gas phase.
items.why: The dot-and-cross diagram hides the energetics. Lattice enthalpy is where ionic compounds get their stability.

items.title: The element you breathe and the element that protects you are the same element
items.claim: Atmospheric oxygen is O2 — diatomic, paramagnetic, essential for respiration. Ozone is O3 — pale blue, pungent, toxic at ground level, and shields the planet from UV. Both are pure oxygen.
items.prompt: Why do ozone and oxygen behave so differently?

options.text: Ozone contains a heavier isotope of oxygen
Three-atom O3 has a bent structure with delocalised pi bonding that absorbs UV strongly (200-310 nm); two-atom O2 has different MO energies and no comparable absorption
The two are not the same element after all

items.reveal:
Ozone is bent (about 117 degrees) with three resonance structures and bond order 1.5 per O-O bond. Its electronic transitions absorb the Hartley band (200-310 nm) strongly — almost all the Sun's biologically damaging UV-B and UV-C.

This is why the Montreal Protocol (1987) was such an unusually successful environmental treaty: CFCs were depleting stratospheric ozone, and replacing them has allowed the ozone layer to begin to recover.

Ground-level ozone produced by photochemical smog is toxic to lungs at parts-per-billion. Same molecule, life-saving at 30 km up, lung-damaging at the surface.
items.why: Allotropes of an element are not minor variants. They can be biologically and atmospherically opposite.

items.title: Endpoint and equivalence point are NOT the same
items.claim: Add NaOH to vinegar with phenolphthalein indicator. The pink colour appears when you've added 'enough' base — that's the endpoint. The equivalence point (exactly stoichiometric H+ matches OH-) is at pH 8.7, not pH 7, and the endpoint depends on the indicator you choose.
items.prompt: Why do you pick phenolphthalein specifically for a weak-acid + strong-base titration?

options.text: Phenolphthalein's transition range (pH 8.2-10.0) brackets the equivalence point of weak-acid + strong-base titrations and lies on the steepest part of the pH curve — so endpoint approximately equals equivalence point

items.reveal:
Titrating ethanoic acid (pKa 4.76) with NaOH gives an equivalence point at pH ~8.7 — not 7. The conjugate base CH3COO- is itself slightly basic and shifts the equivalence point above neutral.

Phenolphthalein (8.2-10.0) brackets this and changes colour in the steep part of the pH jump. Methyl orange (3.1-4.4) would change colour FAR before the equivalence point and give a wrong concentration.

A strong-acid + strong-base titration has equivalence at pH 7 with a very steep jump — almost any indicator works. A weak-acid + weak-base titration has no sharp jump at all and is usually monitored with a pH meter, not an indicator.

Calibration of standards, indicator choice, and meniscus reading all contribute to accuracy of the recorded endpoint volume.
items.why: Titrations are presented as if indicator change marks the answer exactly. The match between indicator pKa and equivalence pH determines accuracy.
